title: upgrade/rollback: transactional downgrade guard, backup/restore, version pinning for private-installer
author: Sofia Martinez
description:
Motivation: Operators running private (VPC/on-prem) deployments have experienced risky manual upgrade paths during schema migrations and image compatibility drift. This PR adds a bundled set of safety mechanisms for upgrade/rollback automation: 1) transactional schema migrations with a downgrade guard that blocks unsafe rollbacks, 2) automated pre-upgrade backup and post-upgrade verification workflows (Helm hooks + off-cluster snapshot tooling), and 3) version pinning and compatibility checks in the Terraform/Helm layers so automated rollouts only proceed when component versions are compatible.

Summary of changes: consolidated upgrade tooling under installer/upgrade, new transactional migration runner (with idempotency and checkpointing), a downgrade guard that consults migration metadata and operator intent, a backup/restore orchestration job (Helm templates + init scripts) that can snapshot Postgres (pg_dump/pg_basebackup options) and object storage, Helm values for version pinning and compatibility matrix, Terraform module checks for required provider versions, and an e2e test harness for the full upgrade/rollback workflow.

Checklist: - [x] Transactional migrations implemented and unit-tested - [x] Downgrade guard logic + operator override flag (--force-downgrade) - [x] Backup/restore Helm hooks and scripts - [x] Version pinning schema and docs - [x] End-to-end test that performs upgrade then rollback on Kind + Postgres replica - [x] Migration docs and operator runbook updated

Migration plan / operator notes: 1) Run preflight: ./installer/cli preflight --target release/v1.8. 2) Trigger backup: ./installer/cli backup --namespace redwood --dest s3://redwood-backups/<cluster>-$(date +%s) 3) Run upgrade with dry-run first: helm upgrade --install redwood ./helm --values values.yaml --atomic --wait 4) If migration step fails, operator can run ./installer/cli restore --source <backup> which will restore DB and reapply previous Helm release. 5) Downgrade guard will abort rollback if irreversible migrations are detected; to proceed the operator must explicitly pass --force-downgrade and provide signed justification (operator must add justification in the vault path or via audit flag).

Testing: added unit tests for migration runner, integration tests that validate checkpointing semantics, and an e2e test (tests/e2e/upgrade_rollback_test.go) that runs a mini-cluster, seeds data, performs upgrade, verifies new schema/kv, then attempts rollback to verify downgrade guard prevents data-lossful rollback unless forced. CI flakiness: e2e requires docker-in-docker; CI now uses a dedicated runner label (runner=priv-installer-e2e).

Risk/rollback: Primary risk is long-running migrations. We added migration batching, max-runtime checks, and automatic pause points with operator notification. Rollback path requires either restoring DB from backup or explicitly forcing downgrade. This PR surfaces both options in the operator runbook.

References: ENG-2345 (upgrade automation), ENG-2410 (downgrade guard design).
